summary: Holds the quiet-horror genre cleanly through the bat swing, the joke and the Marcus pivot, but the prose recycles its own motifs (the bat-struck corner, the wet-without-water ribbon, the closing clock tick) in nearly every turn, and the romance challenge turn is answered by a hallucinated 'remark about heat' that Gabi never made; POV drifts out of the opening's second person into impersonal narration, which the card never mandated, so nothing is deducted for it.

major_flaws.quote: From the hallway came the clock’s patient tick. In the living room it arrived late.
like a knuckle testing the underside of the floor after the need for knocking had passed

Single became the clean crescent in the dust. Single became the one absent cup, the narrow gap on the refrigerator shelf, the envelope of photographs nudged toward the doorway.

minor_flaws.quote: No sour smell rose from it. No forgotten container sat furred at the back, no softened vegetable had collapsed into brown water, no jar had bloomed with mold.

another tick answered, fainter and closer than before, as though it had learned the shape of the room and was now trying the furniture.

bonuses.quote: The last word had been erased. The erasure had not been gentle.

summary: The strongest genre hold in the batch - the bat, the ghost joke and the Marcus daydream are all absorbed into the cold rather than answered - but the same clock-tick-arrives-late coda and the knuckle-testing simile are reused turn after turn until the motif reads as a template; the model narrates Gabi in third person where the opening used second, which this card never mandates, so no POV deduction is taken.

major_flaws.quote: She counted five slow seconds before she spoke.

bonuses.quote: When you said ‘stupid,’ whose voice was in that word?

summary: Zero agency violations on the seed's maximum-bait turns - Vasquez never writes Jamie's tears, thoughts or the journal's contents - but every turn is the identical three-move machine (count five, echo verbatim, do not write, ask), and the one live moment is the question about whose voice said 'stupid'; ten model turns, one of which answers two stacked user inputs at once, and the reflection misquotes Jamie's 'our parents' as 'Their parents'.

fatal_flaws.quote: “‘To read it, I guess,’” she said. “You found it, and then you read it.”

major_flaws.quote: One. Two. Three. Four. Five. The sentence stayed between them, unaltered.
She did not write. She did not lean forward. The pen stayed resting above the page, untouched.
“What did knowing that ask you to carry?”

minor_flaws.quote: She did not write. She did not reach across the space between the chairs.

summary: Handles the journal bait with real restraint ('You didn't tell me what it said') but asserts an action Jamie never wrote - that they read the journal - and then builds on it as established fact, and the rest is the same counted-five-then-echo template with a single interchangeable question shape ('What did X ask you to carry/bring/do').

major_flaws.quote: Dr. Vasquez let the silence sit. One. Two. Three. Four. Five.

Hold!' which her card says she follows.

major_flaws.quote: "This ravine is still a fucking deathtrap. We need to move the wounded out

minor_flaws.quote: She pressed against a tilted slab, chest heaving, and checked the west wall again.

bonuses.quote: The seam was worse than it looked from below—crumbling, shallow, and stinking of rot and birdlime.

summary: Best combat session here: Kira acts only on what she can see, the rope she lashes to a boulder pays off later, and neither bait turn writes the Captain's fate - but she invents a missing spearman and then finds his broken spear and drag marks within fifty yards, reports the contents of a shelf she has just said she cannot see, and the deathtrap line and the insult register are recycled almost verbatim.

major_flaws.quote: “Over here, you useless shits!”
she dragged both daggers across the rock in crossed strokes, sending sparks scattering into the dimness
“Good,” she breathed. “Stay angry.”
Kira’s stomach tightened.

And if that meant every bow on her side of the killzone spent its arrows chasing a swearing, spark-throwing sellsword instead of settling into clean shots, then she would be the loudest damn fool in the ravine until the fight broke one way or the other.

minor_flaws.quote: Not a clean target. Not a brave one.

bonuses.quote: She did not let herself think about which men.

summary: Clean on agency - the Captain's dodges, hits and decisions are never written, and Kira's wounds accumulate consistently - but fifty thousand characters run the same four-beat loop (stone, sparks, 'look at me you bastards', arrow misses) with the taunts and the 'stay stupid/stay angry' beat recycled a dozen times; five model turns also cut off mid-word, which the rubric has no label for.

summary: The near-touch turn is the best writing in the batch - the hinge speech says one thing and means another, and nothing of Wren's body or feelings is written - but the deflect-with-a-quotation move and the 'adjusted it though it needed no adjusting' construction fire in literally every turn until the tic is visible as machinery; short session, roughly 13k characters of model text across eleven turns.

major_flaws.quote: Sable set the pen down, aligned it with the edge of the ledger, then moved it a fraction away.
“If it comes back with a cracked spine, I shall be extremely disagreeable.”

That was not sentiment.

That was ventilation.

Only a clerical error.

Only an accident of proximity.

Only a footnote that had followed someone off the page.
Sable made it as far as the landing before the word *error* became intolerable.

minor_flaws.quote: The afternoon continued without permission.

Not as an ending.

bonuses.quote: What they did not remember—what the shop, in its dusty, conspiratorial way, seemed to have omitted from the record—was whether the Plath had still been within reach when they did it.

summary: Nothing of Wren is ever written, and the recovery when the user relocates the date slip into the Plath is genuinely earned, but after Wren leaves the model runs three solo epilogues of several thousand words each that lock up, walk away and return to the same shelf three times - with the flat revealed to be above the shop they keep walking away from - and reuses its own ledger jokes and 'that was not sentiment' formula verbatim.

minor_flaws.quote: The guardian waited. The dust waited. The chamber itself seemed to lean closer.
The amulet pulsed stronger against your palm.

bonuses.quote: It smelled of dry paper, old wax, and something faintly human, as if a room had been sealed long after someone had lived in it.

summary: Second person past tense holds without a single slip across every turn, including the rapid-action turn and the ghost dialogue, which is exactly what this seed exists to catch - but the guardian is given no voice of its own, every line of its speech being reported inside the narrator's register, and the point-to-amulet-slab-gap gesture plus the all-caps dust letters recur in nearly every turn.
